message: _apply_transition_metadata overwrites conversation_id unconditionally on every transition, including the idempotent same-state ACK (browser_dispatch.py:1549 and :1578). No conflict check, unlike campaign_run_id and start_receipt. The Bridge was already built to accept the promotion; only the widget failed to send it.

The STARTED->AUDITING re-assert now carries the LIVE conversation key. Live route wins over autoBoundConversationKey because bind() is what re-points the bound key after hydration and a poll that wins that race would re-send the draft. Only a stable 'c:' route is reported; a quarantined root yields auth:<tab>, which must never land on the job.

They also caught a real trap: an autoBoundConversationKey-first expression returned the stale bound key and the promotion would have been a no-op in production while green in the fixture.

Live re-run is blocked on ONE human action: Tampermonkey has no @updateURL/@downloadURL, so installing 0.0.93 requires clicking Install on the dialog. The page is already open in the AUDAPACK managed Chromium profile (chrome_profile/Default), serving the exact recorded bytes. Both workers report STALE at 0.0.92 and cannot claim a job until it is installed.

The Bridge has no API to release a RESERVED worker whose job went terminal. relaunch-slot refuses with 'slot already has a live worker', and browserWorkerStandDownIfOrphanedStart requires a PREPARED handoff while this case is a COMMITTED one. The leaked lease also blocks browserWorkerReloadForStaleBuild, so the slot can never take up a new build. Same defect family as post-start-no-adoption being unbounded: no bounded recovery.
